newsitem.title: USA: Dow sheds 100 points as sell programs hit market.
newsitem.headline: Dow sheds 100 points as sell programs hit market.

text.p: U.S. blue chips dropped like a stone in the last hour of trading, shedding nearly 100 points in the biggest point loss since mid-July as investors endured another white-knuckle rollercoaster ride on Wall Street.

"Investors were whipsawed today. They were emboldened at the opening from two fabulous economic reports and then a wave of computer-driven sell orders took the market hostage. Trading is still nervous," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
The Dow industrials lost 1.54 percent to about 6304.

It was a turbulent session that saw the imposition of trading curbs when the Dow fell 50 at 1329 EST/1829 GMT, lifted at 1449 EST as losses were cut and then reimposed at 1521 EST as losses again mounted.
Birinyi Associates Inc tracked five sell programs and one buy that in total erased 96.88 points off the Dow.
It was the largest point drop since July 15's 161.05-point sell-off and followed Wednesday's 71-point loss amid a host of unsubstantiated rumors.
The Nasdaq Composite shed 11 points or 0.82 percent to about 1298.
Losers trounced winners 2-1 on very heavy NYSE volume of about 493 million shares.

Among the Dow's biggest point losers were Disney, off two to 70-1/4, IBM, off 4-1/2 to 151-5/8, 3M, off 2-7/8 to 80-1/4, Philip Morris, off 3-3/4 to 113-7/8, Merck, off three to 76-1/4, and United Technologies, off 2-1/8 to 63-1/2.

Stocks were pressured as a bond market rally withered. After being up one point, the long bond was unchanged in late trading to yield 6.63 percent despite more favorable economic data. Bonds earlier had warmly greeted November retail sales which fell 0.4 percent. A 0.3 percent rise had been expected.

Retailers were mixed, with analysts saying December's retail numbers will be the real measure of the Christmas selling season. A stronger holiday selling season is expected after last year's dismal period.
Sears rose 3/8 to 46-5/8, J.C. Penny fell 7/8 to 49-3/4, Gap fell 1/8 to 30-5/8 and Federated was unchanged at 33-3/8.
Also reported was November consumer prices, up an expected 0.3 percent which followed a benign wholesale inflation report on Wednesday.
Weekly jobless claims fell to 317,000. A 341,000 reading had been anticipated.

"It has become clearly evident that we have already seen the high for the Dow for the short-term. There is a loss of momentum in the stock market," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist of Legg Mason Wood Walker.

As for the latest economic reports, Cripps said, "There's a lot of very, very good expectations already in stock prices. ... The underlying story is that a lot of the stocks that have done the best are the 50 largest caps out there. Most, except for Intel and Microsoft which have robust top-line sales, have earnings that are slowing. A consequence of low retail sales and a subdued economy is (that) earnings will come under pressure."
Bank stocks were hard-hit as bond prices gyrated. Wells Fargo fell 3-1/2 to 264-1/2, Citicorp lost 2-3/8 to 98-5/8 and NationsBank fell 3-1/2 to 92-5/8.

Among individual issues, Warner Lambert rose 7/8 to 76-1/4. Smith Barney upgraded it to buy from outperform after the FDA's advisory panel on Wednesday recommended approval of its drug Rezulin to treat the widespread Type II version of diabetes.
Boston Technology surged 4-3/8 to 23-3/8 after agreeing to supply SBC Communications' Southwestern Bell with $60 million in hardware, software and services.
Tenneco slumped six to 45-1/2.
